name: Burmese Python
habitat: Wet forest, grassland, swamps, river banks and farmland in the plains and foothills, close to water
range: North-east India, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh terai and Uttarakhand foothills; also Nepal, Bangladesh and South-East Asia
diet: Birds, rodents, monkeys, deer and pigs
ids: A very large, heavy constrictor with a pattern of large, rich brown, dark-edged blotches with a light centre on a paler tan or grey background (the pattern is darker and more contrasted than the rock python's).
A spear-shaped, dark arrow mark on top of the head, and a dark streak from the eye to the jaw.
Heat-sensing pits along the lip scales; smooth scales and a short, blunt tail.
Replaces the Indian Rock Python in the north-east and parts of the Himalayan foothills.

look.colour: Tan or grey with dark brown blotches
look.pattern: Large dark brown blotches with light centres
look.head: Triangular head with an arrow mark

fact: Burmese Pythons are the heaviest snakes of the Indian subcontinent. They are protected by law, and in the wild they usually avoid people.

name: Common Sand Boa
habitat: Dry, sandy and loose soil: scrub, farmland, riverbanks, rocky ground and the edges of villages; burrows just under the surface
range: Most of peninsular and western India (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and the Deccan) and Pakistan
ids: A thick, blunt-bodied sand-dweller with a very short blunt tail that looks much like its head, so it is called a "two-headed snake".
Brown, tan or reddish-brown with large dark blotches (often in two rows) along the back; the belly is cream.
Small, flat, wedge-shaped head with tiny eyes and rough, keeled scales.
Slow and docile, and kills its prey by constriction. It is harmless but widely, and wrongly, believed to be venomous.

look.pattern: Large dark blotches in two rows
look.head: Small flat head, tiny eyes, blunt tail
look.body: Short, thick and heavy with keeled scales

fact: The tail of a sand boa looks so much like its head that predators strike the wrong end. In India the animal is trafficked because of the false belief that it brings luck or has medicinal powers.

name: Red Sand Boa
habitat: Dry, sandy and rocky country, scrub, farmland and dry forest; burrows in soft soil
range: Peninsular and central India (Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and the Deccan), north to the Punjab plains
ids: A thick, cylindrical, plain brown, reddish-brown or dark brown snake with smooth, shiny scales and no blotches (young ones sometimes have faint blotches).
A very short tail that is blunt, like the head. Tiny eyes with vertical pupils; the head is a blunt wedge.
Moves slowly and coils into a ball. Harmless, but heavily poached for false beliefs about its magic powers.

look.colour: Plain brown, reddish-brown or dark brown
look.head: Blunt wedge-shaped head and a blunt tail

name: Whitaker's Boa
habitat: Laterite plateaus, rocky scrub and open forest in the north-west of the Western Ghats; burrows in loose soil
range: Goa, Maharashtra (Konkan), Karnataka and northern Kerala (Western Ghats foothills)
ids: A thick-bodied, blunt-tailed sand boa with a pattern of dark, irregular blotches and saddles on a tan to reddish-brown background.
Smaller and with a flatter head than the Common Sand Boa; found in the Western Ghats region.
A harmless constrictor. Similar to the Common Sand Boa, but usually with a more mottled, broken pattern.

name: Indian Rock Python
habitat: Forests, scrub, grassland, rocky hills and swamps, usually close to water; also farmland edges and gardens
range: Most of peninsular India and the Himalayan foothills (the Burmese Python takes over in the north-east); also Sri Lanka, Nepal and Pakistan
diet: Rodents, birds, jackals, wild pigs and deer, swallowed whole
ids: A very big, heavy-bodied constrictor with small smooth scales and a short, tapering tail.
Large, irregular dark-edged blotches in pale brown, olive or yellowish on a tan or grey background; the belly is white or cream.
Spear-shaped pale mark on top of the head and a dark stripe from the eye to the jaw. Heat-sensing pits sit along the lip scales.
Moves slowly and heavily in a straight line and does not spread a hood.

look.colour: Tan, grey or pale brown; white belly
look.pattern: Large irregular dark-edged blotches, spear mark on the head
look.head: Triangular head with a dark streak through the eye
look.body: Very heavy and muscular, smooth scales

fact: A female python coils around her eggs and shivers her muscles to keep them warm, one of the few reptiles that incubates its eggs. The species is legally protected in India.
